findings.summary: Re-entrant read of agent::thread::Thread during a turn trips GPUI's double-lease panic ('cannot read agent::thread::Thread while it is already being updated'), killing the editor on prompt send.

is_ought.is: A read of the Thread entity happens while an update lease is active. EntityMap::lease removes the entity from the map; EntityMap::read then finds nothing and calls double_lease_panic::<Thread>("read").
is_ought.ought: No code path invoked during a Thread update may read the Thread through an Entity/WeakEntity handle (directly or via a callback).

findings.provenance: Direct measurement (live operator log) + Inference (lease mechanism read from source)
findings.evidence:
PANIC at crates/gpui/src/app/entity_map.rs:164:32: cannot read agent::thread::Thread while it is already being updated
(immediately after: INFO [agent::thread] Thread::send called with model: glm-5.3:cloud)
findings.impact: Editor process panics (main thread) on the first prompt of a session; all in-flight work is lost.
findings.root_cause_status: NOT PINNED — the release-build backtrace is all '<unknown>' (no symbols). The synchronous send path (flush_pending_message / cancel / enabled_tools / clear_summary) reads no Thread handle, so the re-entrant read is most likely in a deferred effect, a spawned turn task, a tool initial_title/run, or an agent_ui handler that reads the native Thread while it is leased.
findings.mitigation: 2026-09-19 (DIVERGENCE D67, commit b5ffa5d668): the panic is now self-locating. `EntityMap::read`/`lease` call `double_lease_panic` directly (the prior `unwrap_or_else` closure broke `#[track_caller]` propagation) and `Entity::{read,read_with,update,update_in}` / `WeakEntity::{read_with,update,update_in}` / the `AppContext::{read_entity,update_entity}` trait + production impls (`App`, `Context<T>`, `AsyncApp`, `AsyncWindowContext`) carry `#[track_caller]`; `double_lease_panic` embeds `std::panic::Location::caller()` in the message. A release-build panic therefore names the offending file:line:col — a re-entrant read at `crates/gpui/src/app.rs:3159` now reports '(at crates/gpui/src/app.rs:3159:36)' instead of only `entity_map.rs:164`. Pinned by `double_lease_panic_names_the_offending_call_site` (crates/gpui/src/app.rs); gpui lib suite 332/332 green; `cargo check -p agent` green. The re-entrant read site itself still needs one reproduction with the new message.
suspects: crates/agent/src/agent.rs:1016-1018 cx.observe(&thread_handle, save_thread) -> save_thread reads thread (agent.rs:1977)
crates/agent/src/agent.rs:1546/1571/3465/3877 reads of Thread from subscribe/observer paths
crates/agent/src/thread.rs:4377 tool.run(...) invoked inside the handle_completion_event update — a tool whose run body reads its stored WeakEntity<Thread> before its first await
crates/agent/src/thread.rs:5218-5221 unregister_running_subagent reads sibling Thread entities while the caller holds the parent's lease
agent_ui thread_view.rs:1806-1829 AcpThread::send -> NativeAgentConnection::prompt -> Thread::send nesting
findings.fix_suggestion: Reproduce once with the D67 self-locating panic: the message now names the offending file:line:col directly, so the fix is to move that read out of the update — capture the value from the already-borrowed &Thread, or defer with cx.defer (the pattern already used in crates/swarm_panel/src/swarm_panel.rs:681-691). No symbolicated build is needed anymore.
findings.pattern_signature: double_lease_panic::<T>("read") / '.read(cx)' or 'read_with(cx' on an entity handle reachable from inside that same entity's update closure; kask precedent fix comment: 're-entrant read triggers double_lease_panic'

is_ought.is: grep over the whole repo shows thinking_sender defined once (thread.rs:7156) with no callers; the only send of ToolCallThinking is inside thinking_sender itself (thread.rs:7162); the only consumer is agent.rs:2594 -> AcpThread::append_tool_call_thinking.
is_ought.ought: Either the live tool-call thinking trace has a producer (skill execution), or the consumer plumbing and its comments must be removed — a documented capability with no producer is misinformation. Per .rules, stale comments are active misinformation.

findings.summary: StreamAccumulator silently converts an unparsable text tool-call input into JSON null, discarding the parse error.

is_ought.is: LanguageModelToolUseInput::Text(text) => serde_json::from_str(text).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null) — a malformed tool-call argument string becomes Null with no error surfaced.
is_ought.ought: Per .rules, a fallible operation must not silently discard its error; the caller should surface the parse failure (or preserve the raw text) so malformed arguments are distinguishable from an intentional empty object.

findings.impact: A downstream tool sees Null args instead of the raw malformed payload; the failure looks like an empty call, masking provider/stream corruption.
findings.fix_suggestion: Surface the parse error (e.g., structured tool_call with an error field) or preserve the raw text; do not collapse to Null.

findings.summary: build_request_with_images collapses a documented 'tool' ChatMessage role into Role::User; no production caller exercises it today.

is_ought.is: let role = match m.role.as_str() { "system" => Role::System, "assistant" => Role::Assistant, _ => Role::User }; so a "tool" role message (documented at hkask-types/src/ports/inference_types.rs:17) is sent to zed as Role::User.
is_ought.ought: The role mapping must be explicit about every documented role; silently treating tool results as user turns changes conversation semantics. If zed's Role genuinely lacks Tool, the collapse must be documented at the mapping, not implied by `_`.

findings.provenance: Direct measurement (source read) + Inference (Role enum has no Tool variant: crates/language_model_core/src/role.rs:6-10)
findings.impact: Latent: the doc comment above the function claims tool-role messages are handled ('supports 4 roles: system, user, assistant, tool'), which is not what the mapping does.
findings.fix_suggestion: Make the role mapping exhaustive and comment the deliberate tool->user collapse (or reject tool role explicitly). Needs investigation of whether zed can represent tool results.
findings.pattern_signature: match role { 'system' => System, 'assistant' => Assistant, _ => User }  // catch-all swallows an enumerated role

findings.summary: Corpus batch/OCR concurrency state panics on a poisoned std::sync::Mutex, turning one panic into a cascade that kills all subsequent batching/OCR work.

is_ought.is: self.inner.state.lock().expect("adaptive limiter state mutex poisoned") (and the OCR health-state equivalent) — a poisoned lock aborts the call.
is_ought.ought: Per .rules (no unwrap/panic in library code) and for consistency with the same codebase's deliberate poison recovery (kask_bridge/src/inference_chat.rs:522 .unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner())), a poisoned lock should be recovered or surfaced as a typed error, not panic.

findings.evidence:
batch.rs:233  .expect("adaptive limiter state mutex poisoned")
llm_ocr.rs:174  let mut state = self.state.lock().expect("OCR health state mutex poisoned");
findings.impact: Any panic while holding the lock (or a prior panic in the process) permanently poisons it; every later acquire panics, so the MCP server's batch concurrency and OCR health tracking are unrecoverable without a restart.
findings.fix_suggestion: Recover with unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) where the guard is a simple counter, or convert to a typed McpToolError; at minimum log the poison once rather than panicking per call.

observations.summary: The corpus QA grounding gate's admission policy was reversed (model_inference answers are now admitted and persisted) but the authoritative D9 seam record still documents the old policy ('model_inference answers fail closed') and cites a pin that no longer exists.

is_ought.is: verify_grounding_gate requires every cited_substring claim to be strength 2 and at least one to exist, then records the answer's provenance (tool_verified | model_inference) and ADMITS the row either way (qa_grounding.rs:808-847). The ingest tool description (tools/corpus.rs:172) and corpus.md were updated to match; commit ed9be534cc did not touch DIVERGENCE.md.
is_ought.ought: The authoritative seam record and the enforcement line must agree. If the reversal is deliberate, D9 must be updated (policy sentence + the deleted pin name `model_inference_cannot_be_ingested_as_verified`) and the operator ruling / independent semantic oracle the old policy required must be named; otherwise the gate has regressed.

observations.provenance: Direct measurement (source + seam record + git history) + Inference (policy intent read from the D9 text)
observations.evidence:
DIVERGENCE.md D9: 'admits only rows whose applicable factual claims are all strength 2 — model_inference answers fail closed (V1 intentionally blocks paraphrase and conceptual answers until an independent semantic oracle is specified...)'; pins: '...model_inference_cannot_be_ingested_as_verified...'
qa_grounding.rs:808-812: '// Admission rests on the row's evidence: every cited_substring claim must be byte-verified (strength 2) and at least one must exist. The answer may be a synthesized model_inference observation; it is admitted on the citations...'
observations.impact: The authoritative integration record contradicts its own enforcement line and cites a test that no longer exists (grep finds `model_inference_cannot_be_ingested_as_verified` only in DIVERGENCE.md). Downstream, model-synthesized answers now enter the training JSONL / QA h_mems (labelled answer_provenance=model_inference) without the independent semantic oracle the prior operator-approved policy required. At the next rebase or audit, a deliberate change and drift are indistinguishable.
observations.fix_suggestion: Operator adjudication required: if ratified, update D9's policy sentence and pin list (name the new pin `model_inference_answer_is_admitted_and_persisted_as_model_mediated`, the operator ruling, and the oracle); if not ratified, restore fail-closed admission. Do not silently edit the record either way.
observations.pattern_signature: seam record's policy sentence contradicted by the enforcement function; pin list cites a deleted test name (grep the pin name: only the seam doc matches)

lessons_learned: The live thinking trace users see is the model's own reasoning (LanguageModelCompletionEvent::Thinking -> ThreadEvent::AgentThinking -> AcpThread thought block); the per-tool-call thinking trace is dead plumbing left over from the removed skill cascade. Future probes of 'thinking' should separate these two paths before looking for bugs.

The in-process pivot (DIVERGENCE D8) removed the skill-cascade executor but left both its consumers (ToolCallThinking pipeline) and its comments ('used by skill execution') in the tree. Grep the PRODUCER, not the consumer, when validating an advertised capability.

GPUI double-lease panics are a recurring class in this fork with a documented local fix pattern (crates/swarm_panel/src/swarm_panel.rs:681-691). Any new code that reads an entity handle from inside that entity's own update reintroduces it. Release builds carry no symbols, so the panic message itself must carry the call site: D67 added `#[track_caller]` propagation + `Location::caller()` to the read/update/lease chain.

The corpus crate's error handling is unusually disciplined: near-zero production unwraps outside LLM-output parsing, and the grounding/ingest gate re-executes rather than trusting artifacts. The remaining panic surface is mutex-poison expects in the concurrency helpers (batch.rs, ocr/llm_ocr.rs).

A gate whose policy changes must have its seam record changed in the same commit: ed9be534cc reversed the corpus grounding gate (model_inference answers now admitted) and updated the crate docs and ingest tool description, but not DIVERGENCE.md D9 — which still says 'fail closed' and still lists the deleted pin `model_inference_cannot_be_ingested_as_verified`. When probing a gate, always diff the seam record's policy sentence and pin list against the enforcement function; the pin list is the fastest drift detector (grep each pin name).
